title: Vector: Anti-gravity racing v1.00 Released! Free to play!
author: MrPipUK
selftext:
VECTOR has hit 1.00 🚀

Really proud of this one: anti-gravity racing at 700+ km/h, free in your browser.

5 circuits (one on the Moon), 5 craft, a 72-event career, 31 achievements and online races for up to 8.

Come and race me 👇  
https://wavedash.com/games/vector-anti-gravity-racing

\#indiedev #gamedev

replies.author: W2DGAMES
replies.body:
Interesting take, especially given your own posts about wanting to develop a Star Fox/Mario Kart-style racing game.

You've openly discussed how difficult it is to get the mechanics, level design, scope and replayability right, so I'd have thought you'd appreciate the work involved in taking something from an idea to an actual playable release.

I also notice you've made almost identical comments on other AI-developed games, usually questioning whether they'll still be fun after a few minutes.

That's a perfectly legitimate design question, but "the level design always sucks on these" isn't really constructive criticism, is it?

I'm happy to discuss Vector's design decisions and genuinely welcome feedback. But there's a difference between identifying a problem you've experienced and simply assuming a game isn't enjoyable because of how it was developed.

You've got some interesting game ideas yourself. Hopefully you'll get to bring one to release, because I think you'll find it's rather different being on this side of the conversation.
